findings.where: Screen 13 (Mixed: twenty steps), picture at 360 px and 1280 px before Check
findings.what: The y axis runs straight through the label '(1, −1), λ = 0.5', so its minus sign reads as a cross ('(1, ┼1)'), and that is the one label the puzzle turns on; place it clear of the axis, for example at the lower-right end of its line.

findings.where: Screen 11 (Too few eigenvectors), text plus the act line under the picture
findings.what: The screen carries 107 words (89 in the text, 18 in the act line), well over about 90; drop the act line's second sentence, since the greyed switch and its reason are already in view, and trim one sentence from the 2I ending.

findings.where: Screens 1, 3 and 9, text plus act line
findings.what: With their act lines these screens show 99 to 101 words, all at or past the 90-word limit, so each could hand one sentence to the picture, for example 'A dot marks the top of its pole' on screen 1, which the dot's label already shows.

'Each step only stretches, so it multiplies the first amount by 3 and the second by 2' skips why the amounts change separately: A acts on a mix part by part, so A(a(1, 0) + b(−1, 1)) = 3a(1, 0) + 2b(−1, 1); the explain says this, but no screen does.

findings.where: Screen 7 (Many steps at once), text, and screen 8's Why?
findings.what: The text jumps from Aⁿ = PDⁿP⁻¹ to Aⁿ = [3ⁿ 3ⁿ − 2ⁿ; 0 2ⁿ] without the one multiplication that gets there (PDⁿ = [3ⁿ −2ⁿ; 0 2ⁿ], then times [1 1; 0 1]), and screen 8's Why? states PD³P⁻¹ = [27 19; 0 8] with no working either.

It gives the pump's eigenvalues and the 200 and 400 split without a quick check, A(3, 2) = (3, 2) and A(1, −1) = (0.5, −0.5), and never says that 200 lots of (3, 2) is (600, 400), which is why tank 1 heads for 600 L.

findings.where: Screen 5 (Into the grid and out again), middle panel
findings.what: The square amounts panel labels its axis ends '(1, 0)' and '(−1, 1)', which read as points sitting there rather than as 'lots of (1, 0)' and 'lots of (−1, 1)', so name the axes that way.

findings.where: Puzzle screens such as 2 and 13, at 360 px and 1280 px before Check
findings.what: About 70 to 80 px of blank space sits between the pane and the key, kept for the working row that appears after a right answer, so the opening picture looks unfinished.

findings.where: Key under the picture on screens 11 and 13
findings.what: Key items that are hidden ('the dot’s amounts', 'each step') still take their room, so the visible 'eigenvector line' entry sits well left of centre.

The cards open on A⁰ = [1 0; 0 1] and D⁰ = [1 0; 0 1] before any sentence says that zero steps leaves every arrow where it is; a short card note or one clause would stop him wondering where the identity came from.
'A repeated eigenvalue needs two independent eigenvector lines' reads as a rule about eigenvalues; say 'To be written as PDP⁻¹, a 2 by 2 needs two independent eigenvector lines'.

'Charge flows all the time, not in jumps once a second' is not where the analogy breaks, because it only looks once a second and the step rule is exact at each look; keep the leakage point and say instead that the rule says nothing about what happens between looks.
'Then each sequence can be worked on its own' uses 'sequence' without saying what it is, so name the positive, negative and zero sequences once or just say 'each part'.

findings.where: Whole lesson against the brief (screens 9 and 11)
findings.what: The brief promised symmetrical components named on one screen, and the names algebraic and geometric multiplicity for the shear, but no screen carries either, so the only trade link sits in the notes.
